info.title: Octo Docs Bot API
info.description: Bot-facing document metadata surface under /v1/bot/docs: doc lifecycle, members, sharing, comments, versions, and attachment metadata. Live document body/outline editing is a Yjs websocket path and is NOT part of this REST surface.

get.summary: Save the live PPT as a self-contained HTML presentation (reader or higher)
get.description: Pass --output slides.html to save the actual file bytes. Without --output, only response metadata is printed. HTML is an offline player, not editable PPTX or PDF. No external assets or collaboration credentials are included.

get.summary: Read the current PPT deck and its base revision
get.description: Reader or higher. Returns authoritative Bento JSON and baseRevision. Use docs.ppt.edit, not the document/sheet/scene or draft endpoints, to edit an html_ppt document. The HTTP response uses a data envelope; the CLI unwraps it once. Shared Docs lifecycle endpoints return flat JSON.

deck.description: Authoritative Bento deck. The current backend format contract is format=bento/slides and version=1 (BENTO_FORMAT_VERSION). Release probes reject unknown versions; a format upgrade requires a coordinated contract/probe update.

contentHash.description: Advisory content digest; may be absent or empty. Use revision fields for concurrency control.

patch.summary: Apply a PPT edit under a mandatory base revision
patch.description: Writer or higher; changing title requires admin. Send only {baseRevision,deck} from a fresh get. Preserve deck.docId, unknown fields inside deck, and stable slide/element IDs; do not copy the response's top-level docId or contentHash into the request. The backend compiles the JSON difference to normal collaboration operations. A 409 CONFLICT means reread and reapply the intended change, never blindly resubmit the stale deck. Members and permissions cannot be supplied in deck JSON. The HTTP response uses a data envelope; the CLI unwraps it once. Shared Docs lifecycle endpoints return flat JSON.

baseRevision.description: The baseRevision returned by the immediately preceding PPT get

deck.description: The edited bento/slides JSON; preserve document identity and stable slide/element IDs. Text elements use html; code elements use content (never code), grammarName (js/ts/py), fontSize, align, valign and lineHeight. Read back the actual rendered fields.

contentHash.description: Advisory content digest; may be absent or empty. Use revision fields for concurrency control.

post.summary: Create a document, empty or initialized from a PPT template; the caller becomes owner/admin
post.description: Create a document in the verified caller Space. Use docType=html_ppt, title, optional templateId (blank by default), and Idempotency-Key for PPT. Content initialization, metadata and member grants commit atomically.

folderId.description: target folder id (optional; defaults to the space default folder)

templateId.x-octo-enum-hint: The CLI retires pitch/report/lesson for new creation by product policy; existing presentations remain readable/editable. Deploy the matching backend catalogue before using signal/terra/orbital/picnic; until then only blank is compatible. A timed-out create with a retired template cannot be replayed through this CLI: reconcile with docs list / docs search first; do not automatically create with a new key. Run octo-cli skills octo-docs and read ppt.md for rollout prerequisites.
templateId.description: PPT template: blank (server default) or signal, terra, orbital, picnic. The four gallery choices require the matching backend catalogue to be deployed first. The CLI rejects pitch/report/lesson for new creation by product policy (octo-cli issue #174); this is not a claim that a deployed backend rejects them. Existing presentations can still be read and edited.

schema.description: Flat creation receipt, not wrapped in data. PPT-specific fields are optional on this shared endpoint. The example is a synthetic fixture of the backend PPT creation contract; see docs/ppt-release-gate.md for source provenance.

docId.description: Server-generated document ID. New PPT IDs have the form d_ followed by 24 hexadecimal characters; existing document IDs remain opaque to callers.

docType.description: Document type; html_ppt for PPT creation.

templateId.description: PPT only: the selected template ID. Historical Idempotency-Key replay may return a retired ID; this response field is not constrained by the new-creation enum.

draftRevision.description: PPT only: initial draft revision (0 on creation).

snapshotVersion.description: PPT only: initial snapshot version (0 on creation).

editorUrl.description: Editor URL; returned for html_ppt only.

shareUrl.description: Presentation URL subject to document access rules; returned for html_ppt only.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required for PPT creation, comments and version writes; preserve on an uncertain retry.

get.summary: List documents the bot owns or is a member of (page-based)
get.description: Page-based listing scoped to the bot's server-resolved space. Response is {total, items}; there is no cursor, so --page-all does not apply — walk pages with --page/--pageSize.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: filter to a single folder

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: items per page (1-100, default 20)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: sort order by last update

post.summary: Search accessible documents by full-text content
post.description: Full-text search across documents the bot can access. Use --keyword for the query and repeat --doc-type to restrict results to doc, sheet, board, or html. HTML results cover documents registered into docs-backend by a mounted octo-doc publish; docs-backend computes the caller's authoritative visible doc-id set before OpenSearch returns metadata or body highlights. The default response preserves the backend {total, items, nextCursor} object; --page-all follows nextCursor and emits the merged items array.

docType.description: document type filter; repeat for multiple types (doc, sheet, board, html)

cursor.description: opaque cursor from the previous page

octoDocSlug.description: HTML document reference for octo-cli html commands: canonical doc_id for a newly created canonical document, or the retained legacy slug for an old document.

delete.summary: Delete a document (forbidden for bots, including owner/admin)
delete.description: Bots must not invoke this operation, even for documents they created or own/administer. The docs-backend bot-deletion policy returns HTTP 403 bot_delete_forbidden, including already-deleted retries. Do not retry, change uid/owner/Space/credentials, or switch to HTML/raw API routes. Ask a human with document admin permission to delete it in Octo. Bot creation, editing, and separately permitted subresource operations are unchanged.

403.description: Bot document deletion is forbidden, including owner/admin and already-deleted retries

get.summary: Export a whiteboard's live scene as PNG, SVG, or portable Excalidraw (needs reader)
get.description: Exports the LIVE scene of a doc_type 'board'. `--image-format png` (default) and `svg` render on the server; `excalidraw` is assembled locally with referenced attachments embedded for round-trip import and requires --output/-o. For PNG/SVG, without --output the command reports response metadata only. A non-board target returns 409 unsupported_doc_type; an unrecognised format returns 400 invalid_format.
get.x-octo-risk-note: read reflects the server-side effect: this is a GET that renders and returns the live scene as an image without mutating any doc state. The optional --output/-o writes to a local, user-chosen path (client side, analogous to curl -o) and does not change the API risk class.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: image format (one of: png, svg, excalidraw); default png. Exposed as --image-format so it does not shadow the global --format output flag.

get.summary: Read a document's live body + its base version (needs reader)
get.description: Reads the LIVE ProseMirror body of a doc_type 'doc' plus the base-version token that pins the read. Pass that token to `docs content edit` as --base-version so the optimistic-concurrency guard can prove the body did not change between read and write. board / whiteboard bodies are a different Y.Doc shape and return 409 unsupported_doc_type here.

doc.description: the live body as ProseMirror document JSON

schemaVersion.description: ProseMirror schema version the body was decoded with

baseVersion.description: opaque base64 base-version token; pass to `docs content edit --base-version`

patch.summary: Apply an incremental block-op edit to a document body (needs writer)
patch.description: Applies a batch of incremental block ops to a doc_type 'doc' body under a mandatory optimistic-concurrency guard. Pass the base-version token from `docs content get` via --base-version (sent as the If-Match header); the server rejects with 412 base_version_stale if the live body moved since that read. The ops batch is a structured array, so pass it as JSON through --data. Only doc_type 'doc' is accepted (board / whiteboard return 409 unsupported_doc_type). Gates: op count over the max → 413 too_many_ops, a single op's content too large → 413 op_content_too_large, block-path too deep → 400 path_too_deep, missing base version or malformed shape → 400 invalid_body, bad anchor / invalid ops → 422.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: base-version token from 'docs content get' (sent as the If-Match header for optimistic concurrency; required)

ops.description: ordered batch of incremental block edit ops. Each op is one of: insert {"type":"insert","at":{"path":[i,...],"position":"before|after|inside_start|inside_end"},"content":[<ProseMirror block nodes>],"expect":{"type":"<nodeType>"}?}; replace {"type":"replace","range":{"from":{"path":[...]},"to":{"path":[...]}},"content":[...],"expect":?}; delete {"type":"delete","range":{"from":{"path":[...]},"to":{"path":[...]}},"expect":?}. `path` is child indices from the doc root; range endpoints must share a parent. Pass via --data.

200.description: Edit applied; carries the new base version

bytes.description: encoded size of the doc after the edit

baseVersion.description: new base-version token for the next edit

newDocVersionSeq.description: sequence of the auto safety snapshot taken before the edit

get.summary: Read a spreadsheet's live cells, worksheet resources, and base version (needs reader)
get.description: Reads the LIVE flat cell map of a doc_type 'sheet' (keys `sheetId!row:col`, values {v,f,s,p,t}), column-width / row-height overrides (sheetDims), hyperlinks (sheetHyperLinks), merged ranges (sheetMerges), sheet tabs (sheetList), freeze panes (sheetFreeze), shared filters (sheetFilters), data-validation/dropdown rules (sheetDataValidations), and the base-version token that pins the read. Pass that token to `docs sheet edit` as --base-version so the optimistic-concurrency guard can prove the sheet did not change between read and write. Sorting is a raw coordinate rewrite, not a spreadsheet-native sort: reorder the complete selected row block, carry each cell's complete {v,f,s,p,t} shape to its destination, and use null for destinations that become empty. The server stores `f` verbatim and does not re-anchor relative formula references; rewrite them for the destination or do not sort that range. Any state keyed by or containing coordinates stays at its old coordinates, including row dims, data-validation ranges, hyperlinks, merges, drawings, and cell-comment anchors; freeze panes and filter ranges/columns also remain fixed. Remap every affected resource for which you have an authoritative readable/writable surface, or do not sort the range. `sheetDims` is one workbook-level map whose keys may be sheet-qualified: `${logicalId}:c<idx>` / `${logicalId}:r<idx>` targets one tab, while bare `c<idx>` / `r<idx>` addresses the legacy default sheet; reads return keys exactly as stored. Rows hidden by an active shared filter are still returned and a full rectangle rewrite includes them. To sort only visible rows, evaluate `sheetFilters` criteria first and build a sparse permutation that leaves hidden row coordinates unchanged; clearing the filter does not preserve the visible subset. doc / board / whiteboard bodies are a different Y.Doc shape and return 409 unsupported_doc_type here. A whole-sheet read over the 1 MB byte cap returns 413 sheet_too_large; pass --limit and follow nextCursor via --cursor. In paged mode every page is bounded by both --limit and the byte cap; sheetDims, sheetHyperLinks, sheetMerges, sheetList, sheetFreeze, sheetFilters, sheetDataValidations, and sheetConditionalFormats are returned on the first page only. When checkbox metadata exceeds the size or inspection budget, 413 includes baseVersion and repairDataValidationKey in the CLI error detail; delete that exact internal key with a validation-only PATCH and retry until the read succeeds. A --cursor whose snapshot moved returns 409 sheet_changed; a malformed --cursor returns 400 invalid_cursor; a non-positive --limit returns 400 invalid_limit. Also returns sheetConditionalFormats for conditional-format rule management.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: max cells per page; opts into paged reads. Bounded by the server byte cap regardless. Omit for a whole-sheet read.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: opaque nextCursor from the previous page; also opts into paged reads. A cursor whose snapshot moved returns 409 sheet_changed.

200.description: Live cells + dims + base version (paged when --limit/--cursor is set)

sheetCells.description: flat cell map keyed `sheetId!row:col`; each value is {v?,f?,s?,p?,t?}. Rows are 0-based and may be 0..9999; columns are 0-based and may be 0..99. A page slice in paged mode. Shrinking rowCount or columnCount retains cells beyond the visible boundary for undo/regrowth, so renderers and exporters should ignore rows >= the effective rowCount and columns >= the effective columnCount.

sheetDims.description: column-width / row-height overrides in one workbook-level map. Keys `${logicalId}:c<idx>` / `${logicalId}:r<idx>` target a specific tab; bare `c<idx>` / `r<idx>` address the legacy default sheet. Reads return keys exactly as stored. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetHyperLinks.description: cell hyperlinks keyed `${sheetId}!${linkId}`; each value is {id,row,column,payload,display?}. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetMerges.description: merged cell ranges keyed `${logicalId}:sr:sc:er:ec` (0-based startRow:startCol:endRow:endCol); each value is true. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetList.description: sheet tabs / pages keyed by logicalId; each value is {name,order,rowCount?,columnCount?}. rowCount is 1..10000 and columnCount is 1..100. The current backend stores explicit counts when it creates a new sheet, defaulting to 200 rows by 20 columns (A-T); missing stored counts therefore identify a pre-existing legacy 1000-row by 100-column sheet. The first tab's logicalId is 'default'. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetFreeze.description: freeze panes keyed by logicalId; each value is {startRow,startColumn,xSplit,ySplit}. An unfrozen axis reads back with startRow/startColumn -1 even when the write used 0. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetFilters.description: shared auto-filter state keyed by logicalId; each value is {ref,filterColumns?:[{"colId":<absolute 0-based column>,"filters":{"filters":[<raw values>]}}],enabledColumns?:[<absolute 0-based column>]}. ref.startRow is the header row and stays visible; criteria apply to rows below it. enabledColumns is non-empty when present, contains only columns inside ref, and identifies the exact columns with visible filter buttons; every filterColumns colId also appears in enabledColumns. It is deduplicated and sorted on readback. For example, ref G:M plus enabledColumns:[6,12] enables only G and M, not H-L. This controls filter-button visibility only, not read or write access. Omitted enabledColumns identifies a legacy snapshot where every column in ref is enabled. An empty filterColumns array is omitted on readback. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

sheetDataValidations.description: data-validation arrays keyed by logicalId; each array can contain every returned validation family, including `list`, `listMultiple`, and `checkbox`. This public shape is not the internal flat `${logicalId}!${uid}` Y.Map. Dropdown formula1 is the serialized option list and formula2 is the comma-separated option-color list. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

baseVersion.description: opaque base64 base-version token; pass to `docs sheet edit --base-version`

hasMore.description: paged mode: more cells remain after this page

nextCursor.description: paged mode: opaque cursor for the next page (null when hasMore is false); pass back via --cursor

sheetConditionalFormats.description: Compact conditional-format rules keyed by logicalId!cfId. Each value is {priority,rule:{cfId,stopIfTrue,ranges,rule}}; the inner rule uses Univer highlightCell, colorScale, dataBar or iconSet. Never expand a rule into per-cell styles. Requires the paired conditional-format API backend. Returned on the first page only in paged mode.

patch.summary: Apply a batch sheet edit — cells, layout, filters, validation, and dropdowns (needs writer)
patch.description: Applies one atomic spreadsheet batch under a mandatory optimistic-concurrency guard. Pass the base-version token from `docs sheet get` via --base-version (sent as If-Match); stale writes return 412 base_version_stale. Existing surfaces are cells, dims, drawings, hyperlinks, merges, and sheets. P0 worksheet resources are: freeze `{logicalId:{startRow,startColumn,xSplit,ySplit}|null}`, filters `{logicalId:{ref:{startRow,startColumn,endRow,endColumn},filterColumns?:[columns],enabledColumns?:[absoluteColumnIds]}|null}`, and dataValidations `{logicalId:[rules]|null}`. The public dataValidations and sheetDataValidations shapes are per-sheet arrays for every validation family, including list, listMultiple, and checkbox; do not send the internal flat `${logicalId}!${uid}` Y.Map shape except for the server-directed deletion-only repair described below. The server requires each rule uid to be unique within the sheet, 1–128 characters, free of `!` and control characters, plus at least one non-empty ranges entry. Checkbox ranges must not overlap another checkbox rule after the complete edit; list and listMultiple overlaps are accepted by the backend and should be sent only when intentional. For a working colored `list` or `listMultiple` dropdown, also send type, formula1 (JSON-serialized option labels), formula2 (the same number of comma-separated colors), showDropDown, and renderMode; omit operator. A listMultiple cell stores its selected labels as a JSON-array string, while a list cell stores the label directly. dataValidations is replace-style per logical sheet: read sheetDataValidations first and resend every rule to keep, but do not write if the deployed read surface omits any validation family on that sheet. null removes a freeze/filter/resource entry, and null or [] removes all validation rules for that sheet. An empty filterColumns array is omitted on readback. When enabledColumns is present it must be a non-empty list of absolute 0-based columns inside ref and select exactly which columns show filter buttons; every filterColumns colId must also appear in enabledColumns. A mismatch or enabledColumns:[] is rejected with 422 sheet_cell_invalid. The server deduplicates and sorts enabledColumns. For example, ref G:M with enabledColumns:[6,12] enables only G and M, not H-L. This controls filter-button visibility only, not read or write access; use protected ranges for access control. Filters are replace-style per logical sheet: read sheetFilters first and resend the complete filter object, including enabledColumns, when changing criteria. Omitting enabledColumns invokes legacy all-columns-in-ref behavior and silently widens the visible controls. An unfrozen freeze axis accepts startRow/startColumn 0 but normalizes it to -1. Sorting is a raw coordinate rewrite, not a spreadsheet-native sort: reorder the complete selected row block, carry each cell's complete {v,f,s,p,t} shape to its destination, and use null for destinations that become empty. The server stores `f` verbatim and does not re-anchor relative formula references; rewrite them for the destination or do not sort that range. Any state keyed by or containing coordinates stays at its old coordinates, including row dims, data-validation ranges, hyperlinks, merges, drawings, and cell-comment anchors; freeze panes and filter ranges/columns also remain fixed. Remap every affected resource for which you have an authoritative readable/writable surface, or do not sort the range. `sheetDims` is one workbook-level map whose keys may be sheet-qualified: `${logicalId}:c<idx>` / `${logicalId}:r<idx>` targets one tab, while bare `c<idx>` / `r<idx>` addresses the legacy default sheet; reads return keys exactly as stored. Bare and prefixed keys for the default sheet are separate entries; when migrating a legacy key, read sheetDims and clear the bare twin in the same batch, for example `{"c0":null,"default:c0":200}`. Rows hidden by an active shared filter still participate in a full rectangle rewrite. To sort only visible rows, evaluate `sheetFilters` criteria first and build a sparse permutation that leaves hidden row coordinates unchanged; clearing the filter does not preserve the visible subset. Any one surface may be the only non-empty batch member, but at least one surface must be non-empty. Only doc_type 'sheet' is accepted. Gates: validation-rule count over the max → 413 too_many_data_validations; cell/dim/drawing count over the max → 413 too_many_cells; worksheet-resource key count over the max → 413 too_many_sheet_resources; a single cell's payload too large → 413 cell_too_large; missing base version, malformed shape, or all batches empty → 400 invalid_body; a cell/dim/drawing/hyperlink/merge/tab/freeze/filter/data-validation violating its contract or key shape → 422 sheet_cell_invalid; writes intersecting a protected range → 403 protected_range. If 413 sheet_too_large includes baseVersion and repairDataValidationKey, submit only `{"dataValidations":{"<repairDataValidationKey>":null}}` with that base version, then retry. The backend accepts this flat-key form only when it deletes checkbox-shaped stored metadata and strictly reduces that metadata; do not invent a flat key. conditionalFormats is a sparse logicalId!cfId map of complete rule upserts or null deletions. Rules are removed with a deleted worksheet. Row/column structural edits on a sheet with conditional formatting are refused until rule relocation is supported.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: base-version token from 'docs sheet get' (sent as the If-Match header for optimistic concurrency; required)

cells.description: batch of cell ops keyed by cell key `sheetId!row:col` (e.g. `default!0:0`). Rows are 0-based and may be 0..9999; columns are 0-based and may be 0..99. Each value is either {"v":<string|number|boolean|null>,"f":"<formula>"?,"s":<style object>?,"p":<rich-text object>?,"t":<number>?} to set the cell, or null to delete it. At least one of v/f/s/p/t must be present on a set. A non-null write at a row index >= rowCount or column index >= columnCount grows that sheet atomically, capped at 10000 rows and 100 columns; a write past either cap is rejected with 422 sheet_cell_invalid. Pass via --data.

dims.description: batch of column-width / row-height ops in one workbook-level map. Use `${logicalId}:c<idx>` / `${logicalId}:r<idx>` to target a specific tab; bare `c<idx>` / `r<idx>` address the legacy default sheet. Bare and prefixed default-sheet keys are separate stored entries: read sheetDims first and clear the bare twin while migrating, for example `{"c0":null,"default:c0":200}`. Each value is a positive pixel number to set, or null to delete that dim. Optional. Pass via --data.

drawings.description: batch of floating-image ops keyed `${sheetId}!${drawingId}` (e.g. `default!img1`). Each value is a serialized Univer ISheetImage — {drawingId (== the key's id), drawingType:0, imageSourceType:"BASE64", source:"data:image/png;base64,…", transform:{left,top,width,height,angle,flipX,flipY,skewX,skewY}, sheetTransform:{from:{column,row,columnOffset,rowOffset},to:{…}}, axisAlignSheetTransform} — or null to delete it. The image bytes ride inline in `source`. A MATH FORMULA is written here too, as a float-DOM drawing: {drawingId, drawingType:8, componentKey:"octo-math-formula", data:{latex,id,fontSize}, transform, sheetTransform} (latex in data.latex; data.id == drawingId). Optional. Pass via --data.

hyperlinks.description: batch of cell-hyperlink ops keyed `${sheetId}!${linkId}` (e.g. `default!lnk1`). Each value is {id (== the key's linkId), row, column (0-based cell anchor), payload:"<url>" (http/https/mailto or an internal #jump), display?:"<label>"} to set, or null to delete. The link lives outside cell data and points at a cell by row/column; put the cell's visible text in that cell's `v`. Optional. Pass via --data.

merges.description: batch of merged-cell-range ops keyed `${logicalId}:sr:sc:er:ec` (0-based startRow:startCol:endRow:endCol, e.g. `default:0:0:1:2` merges the A1:C2 block). Value true to merge that range, or null to un-merge it. Optional. Pass via --data.

sheets.description: batch of sheet-TAB (page) ops keyed by logicalId. Value {name,order,rowCount?,columnCount?} to create / rename / reorder / resize a tab, or null to delete it; name and order are required on every non-null entry, and deleting a tab also removes its validation rules. rowCount is an integer 1..10000 and columnCount is an integer 1..100. The backend stores explicit counts for new tabs, defaulting to 200 rows by 20 columns (A-T); pre-existing legacy tabs without stored counts remain 1000 by 100. On an existing tab, omitting either count preserves that dimension, but a resize payload must still resend name and order. Read the current tabs from `docs sheet get`'s sheetList; the first tab's logicalId is 'default'. To ADD a sheet: set a NEW logicalId here AND write that sheet's cells with keys `${logicalId}!row:col`. Optional. Pass via --data.

freeze.description: batch of freeze-pane configs keyed by logicalId. Value {startRow,startColumn,xSplit,ySplit}; startRow/startColumn are the first scrollable row/column and normally equal ySplit/xSplit when freezing the first N rows/columns. Use -1 for the start coordinate of an unfrozen axis; 0 is accepted there but normalizes to -1 on readback. null unfreezes that sheet. Optional. Pass via --data.

filters.description: batch of replace-style shared auto-filter snapshots keyed by logicalId. Value {ref:{startRow,startColumn,endRow,endColumn},filterColumns?:[{"colId":<absolute 0-based column>,"filters":{"filters":[<raw values>]}}],enabledColumns?:[<absolute 0-based column>]}. ref.startRow is the header row and stays visible; criteria apply to rows below it. colId is not an offset from ref.startColumn. Sending filterColumns:[] keeps the range but omits filterColumns on readback. When enabledColumns is present it must be non-empty, contain only columns inside ref, and select exactly which columns show filter buttons; every filterColumns colId must also appear in enabledColumns. A mismatch or enabledColumns:[] is rejected with 422 sheet_cell_invalid. The server deduplicates and sorts enabledColumns. For example, ref G:M plus enabledColumns:[6,12] enables only G and M, not H-L. This controls filter-button visibility only, not read or write access; use protected ranges for access control. Read sheetFilters first and resend the complete filter object, including enabledColumns, when changing criteria. Omitting enabledColumns invokes legacy all-columns-in-ref behavior and silently widens the visible controls. null removes the filter and all controls. Optional. Pass via --data.

dataValidations.description: replace-style data-validation arrays keyed by logicalId. This public REST shape covers every validation family, including list, listMultiple, and checkbox; do not use the internal flat `${logicalId}!${uid}` Y.Map shape except when the server returns repairDataValidationKey and explicitly requests one deletion-only repair. The server requires each rule to have a uid unique within that sheet (1–128 characters, no `!` or control characters) and at least one non-empty ranges:[{startRow,startColumn,endRow,endColumn}] entry. Checkbox ranges must not overlap another checkbox rule after the complete edit; list and listMultiple overlaps are accepted by the backend and should be sent only when intentional. It replaces that sheet's entire rule set, so read sheetDataValidations first and resend every rule to keep; do not write if the deployed read surface omits any validation family. Checkbox formula1/formula2 are optional distinct literal strings that default to "1"/"0", and the server normalizes allowBlank to true. For a working colored dropdown, use type 'list' or 'listMultiple', formula1 as a JSON string array of labels, formula2 as the same number of comma-separated colors, showDropDown:true, renderMode:2, and no operator. These dropdown fields are recommended rendering inputs, not additional server-required fields. A listMultiple cell stores selected labels in v as a JSON-array string; a list cell stores the label directly. The server strips operator from otherwise-valid list rules. null or [] removes all rules for the sheet. Optional. Pass via --data.

conditionalFormats.description: Compact conditional-format rules keyed by logicalId!cfId. Each value is {priority,rule:{cfId,stopIfTrue,ranges,rule}}; the inner rule uses Univer highlightCell, colorScale, dataBar or iconSet. Never expand a rule into per-cell styles. Requires the paired conditional-format API backend. Sparse upserts: send a complete value to create/update one rule, null to delete it; unrelated rules survive. Read a fresh baseVersion first. Maximum 1000 rules/1 MiB per workbook and 64 KiB per rule. Protected worksheets are checked server-side. Pass via --data.

200.description: Edit applied; carries the new base version

bytes.description: encoded size of the sheet after the edit

baseVersion.description: new base-version token for the next edit

newDocVersionSeq.description: sequence of the auto safety snapshot taken before the edit

post.summary: Insert rows after an existing spreadsheet row (needs writer)
post.description: Inserts count blank rows immediately after the zero-based afterRow in one logical worksheet. The server atomically shifts cells, row dimensions, hyperlinks, merged ranges, drawing anchors, freeze/filter ranges, data-validation ranges, live comment anchors, and protection ranges, then increments sheetList.rowCount. Pass the baseVersion from docs sheet get through --base-version; stale writes return 412 base_version_stale. afterRow is an absolute stored row index within the worksheet's current rowCount, not an ordinal among filter-visible rows. count must be 1..9999 and the resulting sheet cannot exceed 10000 rows. The operation refuses a workbook containing cell formulas with 409 sheet_formula_unsupported because the server cannot safely reproduce Univer formula-reference re-anchoring. Other failures include 403 protected_range, 404 sheet_not_found, 422 sheet_row_out_of_bounds or sheet_row_limit_exceeded, and the normal sheet/document size gates. A worksheet with conditional-format rules is rejected with 409 sheet_conditional_format_unsupported until server-side rule relocation is supported. Never delete the rules automatically to bypass this refusal. Remove the rules explicitly first, or use the frontend.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: base-version token from docs sheet get (sent as If-Match; required)

logicalId.description: logical worksheet id, normally default for the first tab

afterRow.description: zero-based existing row after which blank rows are inserted

count.description: number of blank rows to insert; resulting rowCount must remain at most 10000

post.description: Deletes count rows beginning at zero-based startRow in one logical worksheet. startRow is an absolute stored row index, not an ordinal among filter-visible rows. The server atomically removes resources anchored wholly inside the deleted rows, shifts later resources upward, shrinks intersecting ranges, and decrements sheetList.rowCount. Pass the baseVersion from docs sheet get through --base-version. At least one row must remain. Formula-bearing workbooks return 409 sheet_formula_unsupported; other failures include 403 protected_range, 404 sheet_not_found, and 422 sheet_row_out_of_bounds. A worksheet with conditional-format rules is rejected with 409 sheet_conditional_format_unsupported until server-side rule relocation is supported. Never delete the rules automatically to bypass this refusal. Remove the rules explicitly first, or use the frontend.

post.summary: Find and replace spreadsheet values or formulas atomically (needs writer)
post.description: Finds and replaces every match on the server in one optimistic-concurrency-guarded edit. Pass the baseVersion from `docs sheet get` through --base-version. Scope defaults to the whole workbook; pass logicalId for one worksheet, or logicalId plus an inclusive 0-based range for a selection. range without logicalId is rejected. findBy is `value` by default or `formula`; formula cells can match their cached display value in value mode but are changed only in formula mode. caseSensitive and matchesTheWholeCell default to false. The server trims findString like the spreadsheet UI, treats replacement text literally (including `$` sequences), preserves cell metadata, and reports matchedCells, replacedCells, and total replacements. An empty replaceString is allowed. A stale token returns 412 base_version_stale; protected cells return 403 protected_range; generated batches over the write limits return 413 too_many_cells or cell_too_large.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: base-version token from 'docs sheet get' (sent as the If-Match header; required)

findString.description: literal text to find; leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed and the result must be non-empty

findBy.description: search displayed/raw values or formula source text

caseSensitive.description: match letter case exactly; defaults to false

matchesTheWholeCell.description: require the complete stored value to match; rich-text streams include paragraph terminators and therefore do not match

logicalId.description: optional worksheet logical id; omit for the whole workbook

200.description: Replacement result and current/new base version

get.summary: Read a whiteboard's live scene + its base version (needs reader)
get.description: Reads the LIVE Excalidraw scene of a doc_type 'board' — its `elements` in fractional-index (z-order), the `files` map of image/file refs, and the base-version token that pins the read. Pass that token to `docs scene edit` as --base-version so the optimistic-concurrency guard can prove the scene did not change between read and write. doc / sheet bodies are a different Y.Doc shape and return 409 unsupported_doc_type here; a live scene that decodes to a wrong-kind / corrupt blob returns 409 board_snapshot_invalid.

elements.description: the live Excalidraw elements in fractional-index (z-order); each element is a whiteboard-schema node

files.description: map of fileId -> file ref (e.g. {attachId}) for images/files referenced by the scene

baseVersion.description: opaque base64 base-version token; pass to `docs scene edit --base-version`

patch.summary: Apply an element upsert/delete batch to a whiteboard scene (needs writer)
patch.description: Applies a batch of element upserts and soft-deletes to a doc_type 'board' scene under a mandatory optimistic-concurrency guard. Pass the base-version token from `docs scene get` via --base-version (sent as the If-Match header); the server rejects with 412 base_version_stale if the live scene moved since that read. `elements` are full elements to upsert (CAS: the higher `version` wins), `deletedElementIds` are soft-delete tombstones, and `files` upserts file refs; the batch is a structured object, so pass it as JSON through --data. Every element in `elements` must carry a valid fractional-index `index` (z-order key); the CLI rejects an index-less or malformed-index element locally before sending. Only doc_type 'board' is accepted (doc / sheet return 409 unsupported_doc_type). Gates: element count over the max → 413 too_many_elements, a single element too large → 413 element_too_large, whole scene over the cap → 413 doc_too_large, an element failing the whitelist → 422 board_element_invalid, a file ref with no usable attachId → 422 board_file_invalid, missing base version or malformed shape → 400 invalid_body.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: base-version token from 'docs scene get' (sent as the If-Match header for optimistic concurrency; required)

elements.description: full Excalidraw elements to upsert; on a key collision the element with the higher `version` (then smaller `versionNonce`) wins the CAS. Each element MUST carry a valid fractional-index `index` (z-order key produced by the fractional-indexing / Excalidraw rules, e.g. `a0`); an index-less or malformed-index element is rejected locally before sending. Pass via --data.

deletedElementIds.description: element ids to soft-delete; each becomes a tombstone with a superseding version so it converges under CAS. Pass via --data.

files.description: map of fileId -> file ref (e.g. {"attachId":"…"}) to upsert for images/files referenced by the scene. Pass via --data.

A stale permissionEpoch returns 409 share_settings_conflict: re-read the settings and re-evaluate the intended change; do not blindly retry with a newer epoch. Use --scope restricted for owner/members only, or --scope anyone_in_space --role read|edit for Space access. With restricted, role is ignored and stored as read. Unknown scope is 400 invalid_scope; missing/invalid role for anyone_in_space is 400 invalid_role; a non-admin caller is 403; a missing/cross-space doc is 404; an archived doc is 409. post.summary: Add an anchored root or reply (commenter or higher)
post.description: A reply sets parentId and omits anchors. A root comment needs an anchor. For boards, `docs comments add` accepts --body plus exactly one of --point X,Y or repeatable --element-id; these board anchor flags are mutually exclusive with --data and the reply/rich-document anchor flags, and element-anchor dry runs still read the live scene. Other callers, replies, and advanced scenarios use --data with opaque base64 anchorStart/anchorEnd from a live editor selection, or anchorText for rich documents; ambiguous text anchors fail with 422 ambiguous_anchor and can be narrowed with blockPath/occurrence. For sheets, pass the base64 cell key as both anchors. PPT roots use anchor {kind,versionSeq,baseRevision?,slideId?,elementId?,elementIds?,x?,y?}; replies use parentId only. PPT writes require Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Preview or apply literal text-to-columns (needs writer)
post.description: Defaults to server-side preview; --dry-run only prints the HTTP request and is not a data preview. Read a fresh baseVersion, preview, then apply with --preview=false and that same token. Both input and output are bounded to 20000 cells (or the lower deployed write limit). Active filters, source formulas, intersecting merges, drawings, hyperlinks, validations and comments are refused; protection and authorization are checked server-side. Apply is one atomic guarded sheet edit with an automatic safety snapshot. Preserves leading zeros, long numbers, empty fields and formula-looking text; writes strings with text number format @, while retaining destination styles. Overwriting nonempty destinations requires --overwrite.
